import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_98/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_98/test_1.csv"

# Load source tables
# Source 0 schema: ['right_index', '0']
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path)

# Source 1 schema: ['0']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path)

# Transformation plan:
# Target schema: ['0_x': float, '0_y': float]
# Source 0 has columns: right_index, 0
# Source 1 has column: 0
# The target has two columns named '0_x' and '0_y' which correspond to the '0' columns from source0 and source1 respectively.
# Since source0 has 1000 rows and source1 has 500 rows, and target has 500 rows,
# we will join source0 and source1 on source0.right_index == source1 index (row number),
# because source1 has no index column but 500 rows, and source0.right_index looks like an index.
# After join, '0' from source0 becomes '0_x', '0' from source1 becomes '0_y'.
# We keep only rows where the join succeeds (inner join) to get 500 rows matching target size.

# Reset index on df1 to get a proper join key
df1 = df1.reset_index().rename(columns={'index': 'right_index', '0': '0_y'})

# Rename source0 '0' column to '0_x'
df0_renamed = df0.rename(columns={'0': '0_x'})

# Merge on 'right_index'
df_merged = pd.merge(df0_renamed, df1, on='right_index', how='inner')

# Select only the target columns
target_df = df_merged[['0_x', '0_y']]

# Save to target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_98/target_multisource_cot.csv"
target_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
